messages:
Maria Chen: Quick check — sketching a signal-shaping approach for pool admission. Goal: reduce jittery admits during flash traffic by smoothing the intent signal and adding short dampening windows. Thoughts?

Kevin Patel: Nice. Where does the 'intent' input come from? forecasting service or reactive queue depth?

Maria Chen: intent = forecasting output (short-horizon QPS) + tenant headroom allocation. We blend that with reactive signals (queue depth, recent rejects) so admits don't overshoot when forecasts misfire.

Ashok Rao: Concern: blending can mask real spikes and delay useful prewarms. Propose a rapid unblock if queue depth crosses threshold X for Y ms.

Diane Park: +1. Also need hard per-tenant ramp caps so one noisy tenant can't consume burst budget while others starve. Keep the pool-level headroom budget enforced.

Kevin Patel: Operator boundary note: forecasting & headroom calc stays in control plane; admission decisions (admit/delay/reject) executed in the operator/runtime. That keeps runtime simple and reduces churn on operator code paths.

Maria Chen: Exactly. Operator should accept a small admission policy blob from control plane: stable smoothing window, burst multipliers, and a short blockade rule. Example fields: `smoothing_ms`, `burst_factor`, `blockade_pct_change`.

Kevin Patel: Example admit payload from control plane -> operator: `{\"decision\":\"delay\",\"hold_ms\":200}`. Runtime treats `delay` as a soft backpressure hint and will queue up to N ms before returning reject.

Ashok Rao: Implementation quirk — if forecasts are wrong and we unblock too slowly, tails suffer. Suggest a fast-path: if instantaneous free_slots > prewarm_threshold, force admit even during blockade.

Diane Park: Also add observability: `admit_decisions_total{decision=\"admit|delay|reject\",reason=...}` and `admit_latency_ms` percentiles. Need per-tenant and aggregate metrics.

Kevin Patel: I built a tiny PoC (PR #4822) that emits those metrics and implements `blockade_pct_change`. Runs in staging. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/4822

runtime-bot: deploy 1717779000: canary `signal-shape-v1` started in staging :rocket:

Maria Chen: Can folks run synthetic spike tests: 1k concurrent tiny requests with a few noisy tenants, check headroom bleed, warmup latency, and percent of `delay` vs `reject`. I'll post a test plan.

Ashok Rao: Will do. Add a scenario with forecast dropout (zeroed forecasts for 30s) to see how reactive fallback behaves.

Diane Park: Let's schedule a short sync with infra next Tue — want to align rollout cadence and operator config knobs. I'll create the invite.

Kevin Patel: Sounds good :thumbsup:
